Hi Jane / Tom 

Thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap from our discovery so the team is aligned and we have clear next steps. Please call out anything I missed.

Key pain points you reiterated:
- Customer-facing chatgen feature must hit consistent sub-200ms latency for short prompts (<=128 tokens) at peak traffic. Current infra sees 300-400ms p95.
- Throughput: you expect bursts up to ~250 req/s during peak hours with sustained baseline ~40-60 req/s.
- Tokenization/parallelization constraints: model choice impacts KV cache size and memory footprint for multi-tenant use.
- Security/compliance: network isolation (VPC), KMS-managed keys, and audit logs required for procurement.

Goals we discussed:
- Achieve p95 generation latency <150ms for <=128-token responses for interactive experience.
- Support 200-300 req/s burst capacity with predictable tail latency.
- Deploy in a VPC-private environment (initially us-west-2) with customer-managed KMS and SOC2 evidence.
- Minimize cost per 1k tokens while staying within SLOs.

Technical signals we captured:
- Preferred model family: open Llama2-style 13B or equivalent (you called out cost sensitivity vs. quality).
- Typical response length: 40-120 tokens.
- Peak concurrency per user: 3-5.
- Batchability: low-latency required but we're ok with small batching (up to 4-6) to improve GPU utilization.

Next steps (owner in parentheses):
1) I'll share a technical deep-dive doc with recommended topology, SLO targets, and cost/throughput tradeoffs (Marissa) - attaching now.
2) We should get an infra contact from your side for a short architecture sync next week (Tom / Jane).
3) I'll loop in our security lead for the KMS/network checklist and SOC2 artifacts (Neha) - expect initial packets by EOD Wed.
4) If agreed, we can run a short proof-of-concept (2 weeks) using Redwood Dedicated (reserved pool) in us-west-2 to validate SLOs (Marcus).

Attachments: redwood-tdr-20261129.pdf (technical deep-dive), slo-table-20261129.xlsx (SLO/measurement plan) - see attached.

Thanks - and please confirm availability for a 30-min infra call next Tue/Wed.

Best,
Marissa Cole

Subject: Technical deep-dive: SLOs, model requirements, and recommended topology (follow-up)

Hi Jane / Tom -

Thanks for the quick reply and the scheduling note - we meant Dec 1 / Wed as the options; Tue afternoon PT works for us (I'll send a calendar invite). Below is the consolidated technical deep-dive summary pulled from the attached TDR and our perf bench runs. Consider this the single-source follow-up that you can share with your infra/security teams.

1) SLOs & measurement methodology
- P95 latency target: <150ms for requests with <=128 output tokens (measured end-to-end, request accepted -> lasttoken emitted).
- P99 latency target: <300ms for same token range.
- Throughput target: sustain 50 req/s baseline, support 250 req/s burst for 10-15 minute windows.
- Concurrency target: up to 400 concurrent open sessions across the fleet; per-host concurrency tuning expected.
- Measurement plan: use distributed tracing + server-side token counters; we recommend sampling 1% of requests for full-span traces and 100% for tail-latency metrics. See slo-table-20261129.xlsx for thresholds and test scenarios.

2) Model & runtime recommendations
- Model family: Llama2-13B quantized (4-bit QLoRa / GPTQ profile) provides best cost/quality tradeoff per your sample prompts.
- KV cache: sized for 4k context; we recommend testing 2k vs 4k to evaluate latency/throughput tradeoffs.
- Batch strategy: small dynamic batching (max batch size 6) with latency-aware batching windows (10-20ms) to avoid tail impact.
- Fallback model: smaller 7B variant for extremely high-load times to preserve availability while degrading quality gracefully.

3) Deployment topology (recommended POC topology)
- Dedicated Redwood pool in us-west-2 (dedicated GPU nodes pinned to your VPC via PrivateLink/VPC peering).
- Node spec: 4x A100-80GB equivalent for baseline POC (estimate 3-4 concurrent inference workers per GPU for target SLOs depending on batch config).
- Autoscale policy: maintain baseline pool of 2 nodes; scale out up to 6 nodes for bursts with warm-up prefetching for KV caches.
- Smart routing: route interactive traffic to low-latency nodes, batch non-interactive work to a separate pool.
- Caching: prefix caching for common prompts + in-region KV cache to reduce repeated token compute.
- Network & security: VPC endpoints, customer-managed KMS for keys, audit logs shipped to your Splunk endpoint, and optional private control plane.

4) Perf bench summary & cost estimate (high level)
- Benchmarks run on quantized 13B in-house: avg p95 observed 120-140ms (<=128 tokens) with batch size 1-4 and tuned kernels.
- Cost estimate for 2-week POC (reserved capacity + data transfer + observability): approximate $18k- $25k depending on node sizing and ingress volume. We'll provide a detailed line-item after we agree on GPU sizing and expected token volume.

5) Open questions / risk items
- Cold-start behavior: cold p95 can be 2x warm p95; we mitigate with warm-keeping policies and pre-warming during expected burst windows.
- Tokenization differences: we saw small output-length variance between models which affects token-cost forecasts.
- Compliance: SOC2 package will be provided; Neha will follow up with KMS/network checklist.

Attachments: redwood-tdr-20261129.pdf, slo-table-20261129.xlsx, acme-network-diagram.png

Best,
Marissa
